subject: Request: provisional uptime waiver for experimental encoder pilot
messages:
From: Elena Soto <elena@constructai.com>
To: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Cc: Tom Hall <tom@constructai.com>, procurement@constructai.com
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot ask: provisional uptime waiver for experimental encoder

Hi Aditya,

Thanks again for last week's demo — the experimental encoder variant reduced our vector compute by ~30% on our internal tests and we'd like to run a 6-week pilot in production with a small user cohort (beta_500). Because the encoder is still flagged as "experimental" in your model catalog, our security and product teams need a temporary SLA exemption for uptime and latency guarantees while we validate behavior under real traffic.

What we need: a written provisional commitment that Redwood will not block traffic or throttle beyond agreed soft-limits, and a one-week rollback window if we see unacceptable accuracy/regression. We also want a short runbook for expected latency headroom and a point-of-contact for incidents.

Attached is a short SLO request doc with our desired targets (slo_proposal_constructai_v1.pdf). Can you confirm process, timeline, and any limits on request volume?

Best,
Elena Soto
Head of Product, ConstructAI

(attachment: slo_proposal_constructai_v1.pdf)

From: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
To: Elena Soto <elena@constructai.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 16:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot ask: provisional uptime waiver for experimental encoder

Elena —

Thanks for the clear ask and the SLO doc. I looped in Neha (Head of Reliability) and Karthik (Sales Engineering) to scope an internal assessment. Short answers up front: we can offer a provisional operational agreement for a limited pilot under explicit guardrails, but we need to document expected latency variance and traffic caps, and we require a rollback plan and an incident POC.

Next steps:
- Neha: can you run a quick risk assessment and propose the guardrails and the runbook?
- Karthik: can you confirm the expected qps and token mix for beta_500 so we can align capacity?
- Elena/Tom: can you confirm start date window (we heard Nov 2 — still accurate?)

I'll produce a short delta agreement for legal if we agree to the provisional terms.

—Aditya Rao
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

(Referenced attachment: slo_proposal_constructai_v1.pdf)

From: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
To: aditya_rao@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: Elena Soto <elena@constructai.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot ask: provisional uptime waiver for experimental encoder

Aditya / team —

I reviewed the SLO sketch and did a quick experimental run against the encoder on our staging harness. Findings summary:
- Median token latency increases by ~12% at 95th pct with the experimental encoder under your reported token mix; tail (99th) showed up to 25% variance on long sequences.
- The model occasionally triggers a higher memory footprint path which can cause transient request rejections when hosts are fully loaded.

Provisional acceptance criteria we can offer for the 6-week pilot (subject to signatures):
1) Soft uptime target: 99.0% for pilot traffic (we will not invoke tenant-wide throttles unless documented overload patterns are observed).
2) Latency guardrail: we will maintain median latency within 20% of your baseline and cap 95th percentile degradation at 35% for pilot traffic.
3) Traffic cap: pilot limited to 500 qps aggregate and 5 concurrent spikes of up to 750 qps for 5 minutes each per day.
4) Rollback: 1-week automated rollback window triggered by ConstructAI incident report or by automated quality/regression alerts from Redwood's eval pipeline.
5) Incident POC: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai (Reliability lead) and on-call SRE.

Attached: encoder_latency_runbook.md (runbook + suggested alert thresholds) and a short delta SLO that legal can sign. We'll also instrument extra tracing for the pilot. If you accept these guardrails I'll ask Legal to draft a provisional rider to the master services agreement (MSA).

-Neha
Head of Reliability, Redwood Inference

(attachments: encoder_latency_runbook.md)

Neha / Aditya —

Thanks for the quick assessment and the concrete guardrails. ConstructAI accepts the proposed provisional terms with two asks before we sign the rider:
1) Please add an explicit escalation SLA for P1 incidents during the pilot (response within 15 minutes, update cadence every 30 minutes until mitigation) and a named escalation contact.
2) Can you confirm that pilot logs and traces will be retained for 30 days and that aggregated latency dashboards will be shared daily?

We anticipate starting Nov 2 with a canary tranche (50 users) and then ramping to beta_500 by Nov 9 if early telemetry looks good. Procurement is copied for timing on contract paperwork.

Regards,
Tom Hall
VP Product, ConstructAI
